title: Insert an Element at a Given Position Into a List
required_features: Authoritative OCaml entrypoint name and exact polymorphic signature
Index-domain boundary, including whether index = length denotes append
Negative and out-of-range behavior (exception, option/result, precondition, or another stated rule)
Official examples or other non-solution behavioral cases
semantic_obligations: Source states that an element is inserted into a list at a specified position.
Source states that positions are 0-based indices.
No stronger ordering, multiplicity, boundary, or failure obligation is stated in the permitted non-solution text; such obligations must not be invented.

source_validation.extraction: Only text preceding the unique H2 Solution heading was examined.

contract.reason: Not supportable without inventing an exact OCaml interface and unspecified invalid-index semantics.

test_harness.reason: No source-declared candidate name or type exists to call.
test_harness.oracle_scope: Valid 0-based positions only; the oracle is isolated from synthesis inputs.
test_harness.negative_control: Run with --negative-control; it intentionally asserts [1;2;9] for insertion of 9 at index 1 into [1;2] and must fail.

caveat: No final implementation was authored or labeled synthesized. A later backend must obtain a non-solution authoritative interface/failure-policy addendum before lowering or candidate validation.
